snp3.10:0.2: SN 6:10 contains a shorter, less graphic version of this sutta.
snp3.10:1.3: Kokālika is a bhikkhu, or Buddhist monk; the texts normally refer to monks as “Ven. So-and-so,” and the story that follows explains why posterity withheld that honorific from him. According to SnA, this Kokālika was not the same Kokālika who was one of Devadatta’s followers—though it’s striking, if so, that both Kokālikas expressed the same mistrust of Sāriputta and Moggallāna in exactly the same words (see Cv VII.4.2). It’s also possible the two Kokālikas were the same person, who joined Devadatta’s schism during the interval this sutta leaves between his denunciation of Sāriputta and Moggallāna and the onset of his disease.
snp3.10:3.3: An exaggerated form of address. See Ud 8:7, note 1.
snp3.10:8.1: Reading vassa-satassa vassa-satassa with the Burmese edition. The Sri Lankan edition reads “every hundred years, every thousand years”; the Thai edition reads “every hundred years, every thousand years, every hundred thousand years.”
snp3.10:8.11: The names of some of the worst hells are, perhaps deliberately, ironic. SnA claims these aren’t separate hells at all but simply different stretches of time within the single Avīci hell, though it offers no explanation or support for that claim.
snp3.10:10.3: The word for wickedness, kali, is the same word used for a bad throw at dice—the image picked up in the following verse.
snp3.10:12.4: The parallel version of this sutta at SN 6:10 ends at this point.
snp3.10:13.4: This verse = Dhp 306, and is also found at Iti 48.
snp3.10:26.1: Vettaraṇin literally means “having a battle of twigs/canes.” SnA identifies it with the river of lye-water described at MN 130, which contains a similarly graphic account of hell.
snp3.10:28.2: Reading passati with the Thai and Sri Lankan editions; the Burmese edition has phusati, “touch.”
snp3.10:29.3: A crore is a large number that SnA calculates as ten million.
